root_cause.text: An off-by-one error in the `titsc_config_wires` function of the `ti_am335x_tsc` driver uses a greater-than operator instead of greater-than-or-equal in the bounds check, allowing `wire_order` values equal to the array size to pass validation and result in out-of-bounds access to the `config_pins` array.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the modification from `if (WARN_ON(wire_order[i] > ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)))` to `if (WARN_ON(wire_order[i] >= ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)))`, directly addressing the CVE description which states the original check allowed `wire_order[i]` to equal `ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)`, causing out-of-bounds access when used as an index.

intent_record.how: Ensures that an index value equal to the array size triggers a warning and error return, preventing potential out-of-bounds array access during subsequent operations

vuln_statements.explanation: The vulnerability occurs in the titsc_config_wires function where the loop iterates 4 times (matching the array size). Based on the root cause, there is likely a bounds check using '>' instead of '>=' when validating wire_order values against config_pins array size. This allows wire_order values equal to the array size (4) to pass validation, causing out-of-bounds access. The loop structure at line 79 combined with the array declarations at lines 75-76 (analog_line[4], wire_order[4]) indicates the iteration count matches the array bounds, making any subsequent bounds check using > operator vulnerable to off-by-one errors.
